title: Polynomial time for an iterated Boolean search
statement: Let $t$ map bit strings to Booleans, and let $\mathrm{nxt},x,r$ map bit strings to bit strings. Let $Q$ map a bit string and a natural number to a bit string, and let $F$ map a bit string and a natural number to a Boolean. Fix $a',k',c\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose the functions $s\mapsto[t(\pi_2(\pi_2(s)))]$ and $s\mapsto\mathrm{nxt}(\pi_2(\pi_2(s)))$ are polynomial-time computable, as are $x$ and $r$. Suppose that $|\mathrm{nxt}(q)|\le |q|+2+c$ for every bit string $q$, that $|x(z)|\le |r(z)|$ and $r(z)=Q(z,0)$ for every $z$, and that for every $z$ and every $i<a'(|x(z)|+1)^{k'}$, one has $\mathrm{nxt}(Q(z,i))=Q(z,i+1)$ and $t(Q(z,i))=F(z,i)$. Then the Boolean-valued bit-string function whose output is the one-bit list indicating whether $F(z,i)$ is true for at least one $i<a'(|x(z)|+1)^{k'}$ is polynomial-time computable.
